title: A Birdbath Among the Flowers
description: A shallow garden basin offers visiting birds water for drinking and splashing.
cardDescription: A shallow garden basin offers visiting birds water for drinking and splashing.
focus: The setting is a Birdbath Among the Flowers. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Shallow outdoor basin for feathered visitors
Opposite of deep when describing water
American songbird known for its orange-red breast
To scatter water by striking or stepping into it
Support that holds an object upright
Part a bird spreads to fly

answerNotes.BASIN: A basin is an open container or depression holding water. In a garden fixture, it is the broad bowl below the spray or drinking rim.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.SHALLOW: Shallow means not deep. At a pool, the word describes the water's depth rather than its temperature.
answerNotes.RIM: The rim is the edge around an opening. A flowerpot, glass, and bowl each have a rim, but not all rims are the same shape.
answerNotes.STONE: Stone is a piece of natural rock. A slab is a relatively flat piece, while gravel consists of many smaller pieces.
answerNotes.WING: Wings help birds, many insects, and airplanes fly, but their structures differ. The model-airplane scene uses a fixed surface rather than feathers.
answerNotes.FEATHER: Feathers help birds with warmth and, in many species, flight. Small soft down feathers have a different job from long wing feathers.

words: Shrub known for fragrant clusters of purple or white flowers
Color made by mixing red and blue
Low woody plant with several stems
Place for one person to sit
Group of flowers growing close together

answerNotes.BENCH: A bench normally seats more than one person. It can be used in a park, entryway, or bus shelter without changing that basic meaning.
answerNotes.SCENT: Scent means a smell, often a pleasant one. Flower scents vary, and not every colorful bloom has a strong fragrance.
answerNotes.SPRING: Spring is the season between winter and summer. Weather and the exact timing of flowers vary by U.S. region.
answerNotes.SHADE: Shade blocks direct sunlight. A shaded garden corner still receives some light; it is different from a completely dark room.
answerNotes.BLOOM: Bloom can mean an open flower or the act of flowering. In a flower clue, it does not mean a leafy bud that has not opened.
answerNotes.WOOD: Wood comes from trees and has a grain. Following that grain when sanding usually leaves a smoother surface.
answerNotes.BRANCH: A branch is a woody limb extending from a tree or shrub. A twig is usually a smaller, thinner piece of that growth.

answerNotes.SUN: The Sun is a star. Its closeness makes it look much larger and brighter than the points of light seen at night.
answerNotes.STONE: Stone is a piece of natural rock. A slab is a relatively flat piece, while gravel consists of many smaller pieces.
answerNotes.NUMBER: A number can count an amount or identify something. A telephone number identifies a connection rather than measuring its size.
answerNotes.CIRCLE: A circle is a round line or shape. In a marble game, a drawn circle can mark the playing area.
answerNotes.HOUR: An hour contains sixty minutes. A minute contains sixty seconds; these two relationships are easy to mix up.
answerNotes.LIGHT: Light makes things visible. A lamp produces light, while a mirror mainly reflects light arriving from elsewhere.
answerNotes.GARDEN: A garden is an area cultivated for plants. A single bed or plot can be one part of a larger garden.

answerNotes.LIGHT: Light makes things visible. A lamp produces light, while a mirror mainly reflects light arriving from elsewhere.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.
answerNotes.GLASS: Glass is usually transparent but can also be colored. A glass is a drinking vessel, while glass without an article can name the material.
answerNotes.HANG: Hang means support something from above. A hook, cord, or branch can hold the weight while the object hangs below.
answerNotes.HOOK: A fishing hook catches by its pointed curve. A wall hook is shaped for hanging objects rather than catching fish.
answerNotes.PATH: A path is a route for walking. Stepping stones can mark that route without making a continuous paved surface.
answerNotes.FLAME: A flame is the visible burning region above fuel. A glowing ember is hot too, but it does not necessarily have a flame.
answerNotes.SHADE: Shade blocks direct sunlight. A shaded garden corner still receives some light; it is different from a completely dark room.
answerNotes.NIGHT: Night is the dark part of the daily cycle. Dusk is the fading-light period around the approach of night.
answerNotes.DOOR: A door is the movable panel at an entrance. Hinges let it swing, while a latch or lock holds it closed.

answerNotes.STONE: Stone is a piece of natural rock. A slab is a relatively flat piece, while gravel consists of many smaller pieces.
answerNotes.STEP: Step can name an action or one level of a stairway. In a stepping-stone clue, it concerns placing a foot on the next surface.
answerNotes.PATH: A path is a route for walking. Stepping stones can mark that route without making a continuous paved surface.
answerNotes.BOOT: A boot rises above the ankle. Its sole can leave a tread pattern in mud or snow.
